posts.excerpt: The process behind Artxonic's signature sound — how I blend AI-generated melodic elements with real human emotion, Urdu poetry, and cinematic production techniques to create something entirely new.
posts.body:
When I started Artxonic, I had one goal: create music that feels genuinely human but leverages the power of AI to reach places human creativity alone couldn't.

## The Process

I start every track with a feeling — a *mood*, a memory, or an emotion. I'll write Urdu or Pashto poetry first, before touching any music software. This anchor keeps the track human even as AI tools shape its production.

Then I use AI tools to generate melodic loops, chord progressions, and atmospheric textures. The human step comes in layering, mixing, and breathing emotion into the structure.

## The Result

Tracks like *Dil Gaya Tumne Leya* are 60% AI-generated in their musical foundation, but 100% human in their feeling. That's the Artxonic formula.
posts.title: How I Produce Urdu Lofi Music Using AI + Human Touch

posts.excerpt: From initial discovery calls to final delivery — how I approach brand identity projects, what questions I ask, and the tools I use to create visual systems that last.
posts.body:
Brand identity projects are my favourite type of work at ArtxPremium. There's nothing more satisfying than watching a business transform when it gets a visual identity that truly fits.

## Step 1: Discovery

Before touching any design software, I spend at least 2 hours with the client understanding their *vision, audience, and competitors*. The questions I ask shape everything.

## Step 2: Concept Development

I sketch 3 radically different directions — not variations of one idea, but truly different approaches. This gives clients genuine choices.

## Step 3: Refinement & Delivery

After client feedback, I refine the chosen direction and deliver a complete brand guide including logo variations, color palette, typography, and usage guidelines.
posts.title: Building a Brand Identity From Scratch — My Complete Process

posts.excerpt: A practical breakdown of the AI tools that have genuinely changed how I work — from prompt engineering in Midjourney to automated design generation workflows.
posts.body:
After two years of daily use, these are the AI tools that earned a permanent spot in my workflow — not the hyped ones, the ones that actually save time.

## 1. Midjourney

My go-to for mood boards, concept art, and visual exploration. The key is *prompt engineering* — learning to describe exactly the lighting, composition, and style you want.

## 2. Adobe Firefly

Generative fill inside Photoshop is a genuine game-changer for extending backgrounds and removing objects cleanly.

## 3. Figma + AI plugins

For rapid UI mockups and auto-layout suggestions.

## 4 & 5: ChatGPT and Runway

ChatGPT for copy, naming, and briefs; Runway for quick motion and video tasks. Together they cover 80% of my AI-assisted work.
posts.title: Top 5 AI Design Tools I Use Every Day in 2024

posts.excerpt: Everything I wish I knew when I started selling beats — from licensing types to pricing strategy, platform selection, and how to build a catalog that actually sells.
posts.body:
When I first put beats on BeatStars, I made $0 for three months. Here's what actually changed things.

## The Reality

Most beat stores fail not because the music is bad — it's because they have no *marketing strategy*. Your BeatStars page is a product, not just a music folder.

## What Actually Works

Tagging beats correctly, creating YouTube content showcasing the beats, and building a recognizable brand (hence Artxonic) — these three things moved the needle more than the music quality itself.
posts.title: How to Start Selling Beats Online — What I Learned the Hard Way

posts.excerpt: I've been a contributor on Adobe Stock, Shutterstock, and Dreamstime for over a year. Here's what actually works, what doesn't, and whether it's worth your time as a designer.
posts.body:
Microstock is genuinely passive once you build a portfolio — but it takes 6-12 months before you see meaningful income. Here's my honest experience.

## Platform Rankings (My Experience)

*Adobe Stock* pays the best per download. Shutterstock has the highest volume but lower per-download rates. Dreamstime is slower but worth submitting to for reach.

## What Sells

Corporate scenes, technology themes, and Pakistani cultural content (rare on stock platforms) perform well. Avoid oversaturated categories like sunsets and coffee cups.
posts.title: Earning Passive Income as a Microstock Contributor — My Experience

posts.excerpt: Everybody is scared of AI taking design jobs. Here's my honest take — after using AI tools daily for two years — on what's actually changing, and how to stay relevant.
posts.body:
Hot take: the designers panicking about AI are usually the ones relying on technical execution as their value-add. The designers thriving with AI are the ones who lead with *thinking*.

## What AI Actually Does

AI automates production. It does not automate taste, strategy, client relationships, or creative direction. If your value was "I can make this in Photoshop" — yes, you're in trouble. If your value is "I understand what this brand needs" — you're fine.
posts.title: AI Won't Replace Designers — But It Will Replace Bad Ones

posts.excerpt: The realities of building a creative freelance career from Abbottabad — dealing with international clients, pricing in USD, navigating Payoneer and Wise, and building a reputation from scratch.
posts.body:
Building a creative freelance career from Abbottabad, KPK — not Karachi, not Lahore — is its own specific challenge. Here's what I wish I knew.

## Getting International Clients

Behance, LinkedIn, and Upwork are the three platforms that actually produced results for me. Cold emailing is underrated — I've landed $500+ projects from a single well-written cold email.

## Getting Paid

*Wise* is the best option I've found for receiving international payments. Payoneer works too but has higher fees. Always get 50% upfront — always.
posts.title: Freelancing as a Creative in Pakistan — Real Talk
